Laura / team — below is the proposed empirical benchmarking plan. I ran a quick dry run on our staging cluster (quantized 8-bit LLM variant) to sanity-check test durations; full runs will use dedicated capacity replicating the expected concurrency profile.

Benchmarking plan (summary):
- Objective: measure sustained QPS and tokens/sec for Payframe sample payloads (40–80 token responses). Capture TTFT (time-to-first-token), p50/p95/p99 latencies for first token and for full response.
- Testbeds: Hosted (multi-tenant) vs Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pool; 8x A100-equivalent slices).
- Model/config: open-llm-v2-7B quantized (8-bit), with KV cache and prefix caching enabled. Rishi will propose alternate quantized profiles if needed.
- Workload profile: synthetic mix that mirrors Payframe sample: 70% 64-token responses, 20% 48-token, 10% 16-token (mean 59 tokens).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48 concurrent streams. Hold each level for 10 minutes steady state and measure sustained QPS and tokens/sec.
- Duration & repetitions: 3 repeats per concurrency point, 10m steady-state per repeat; total ~3.5 hours per full sweep.

Preliminary results (staging dry run, single-node):
- Mean tokens/sec (64-token mix): 980 tokens/sec (single ded. slice)
- Peak sustained QPS (64-token responses): 15 QPS per slice at 99% stability for bursty loads
- TTFT (P95) observed: 140ms (single slice); P99 ~ 240ms
- End-to-end full-response latency (P95): 420ms for 64-token responses

Expected production (8x slices, optimized batching & prefix cache):
- Aggregated sustained tokens/sec: ~7.8k tokens/sec (8 * 980)
- Aggregated sustained QPS for 64-token mean responses: ~120 QPS sustained
- Concurrency tolerance: stable up to 48 concurrent streams when autoscaling configured; without autoscale sustained capacity equivalent to 32 streams per 8-slice pool before queuing increases.

Notes on methodology:
- We compute tokens/sec using decoded token counts from model output; TTL warmup period (2 minutes) discarded.
- For unit economics, Monica should apply pricing for dedicated slices vs hosted metered runs and include caching efficiency assumptions (we expect ~12% effective token-level cache hit for repeated prefixes).

I'll run the full sweep on dedicated dev cluster tonight and upload CSVs. Attaching the result skeleton.

—Marcus
Principal Performance Engineer

Attachments: throughput_results_summary.csv (skeleton), sample_load_profile.json

Subject: Payframe MAP v1 — performance findings & next steps

Sam / Priya —

Attached is the Payframe MAP v1 (payframe_map_v1.xlsx) which includes the evaluation plan and the first empirical benchmarking results from our dedicated staging sweep. Summary highlights below (TL;DR for procurement & engineering):

Key results (dedicated 8-slice pool, quantized 7B variant):
- Sustained aggregated tokens/sec: 7,840 tokens/sec (post-warmup)
- Sustained QPS (mean 64-token responses): 122 QPS (sustained, 95% stability)
- TTFT (P95): 150 ms; TTFT (P99): 260 ms
- End-to-end response latency (P95): 460 ms for 64-token responses

Unit economics (monetized in appendix):
- Baseline metered hosted estimate: ~$0.90 per 1M tokens (public estimate for this variant)
- Dedicated 8-slice committed estimate: ~$0.42 per 1M tokens (assumes 70% utilization over month)
- Estimated cost per auth (mean 59 tokens output + 30 tokens input = 89 tokens total):
  - Hosted: ~$0.0080 per auth
  - Dedicated (committed): ~$0.0037 per auth
- At 1M auths/month: hosted ~$8,000/month; dedicated ~$3,700/month (not including reserved capacity platform fee)

MAP next steps & go/no-go criteria:
- Engineering go: P95 TTFT < 200 ms and sustained QPS > 100 for typical 64-token responses.
- Procurement go: Signed PO + commitment to a 3-month dedicated pool trial (or month-to-month with overage caps)
- Schedule: Send PO for dedicated trial by 2026-03-05 to start provisioning week of 3/9.

Deliverables sent: payframe_map_v1.xlsx (MAP + appendices), throughput_results_summary.csv (detailed CSV of runs), sample_load_profile.json. Links to HubSpot deal and DocuSign in the MAP cover sheet.

Questions / requests:
- Sam: please confirm the sample payloads reflect your production mix (we used 70% 64-token). If you have a different mix, send the sample JSON and we'll re-run.
- Priya/procurement: if you want a pricing appendix that compares 6- and 12-month committed discounts, Monica can add that in v2.

Thanks — look forward to your feedback.

Laura Bennett
